assumptions: The service is evaluated at the planning stage, with no inferred customer contracts, traction, proprietary data rights, or validated unit economics beyond the supplied evidence.
Accredited verification and exceptional supplier work remain prepaid third-party add-ons rather than services or liabilities absorbed in the base offer.
The founder can lawfully develop the analytical workflow from public rules and customer-provided shipment exports without using confidential employer resources.
The proposed prices, delivery hours, CAC, margins, and renewal targets are hypotheses rather than demonstrated performance.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid pilots with several in-scope importers should establish the budget owner, diagnostic price, sales cycle, fully loaded CAC, delivery and support hours, contribution margin, and conversion to a paid second cycle. Evidence should also quantify when the default-versus-actual analysis changes a decision or saves more than the service and verification cost, and include signed data-use and retention rights plus at least one repeatable direct or referral acquisition channel.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The redesign identifies a real, certificate-linked decision: whether actual supplier emissions and accredited verification are worth their incremental cost versus Commission defaults. This is more focused and controllable than open-ended supplier chasing, but the insight is accessible to brokers, software vendors, and enterprise systems.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: CBAM creates measurable cash exposure and recurring compliance work, and a named importer has adopted an external CBAM solution. However, no evidence shows willingness to buy this distinct decision service, its price tolerance, its budget owner, or how often the analysis produces material economic value beyond defaults or existing tools.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Fixed scope, advance billing, capped support, and prepaid specialist work can limit working-capital and delivery risk. Yet every decisive economic variable is unvalidated, including realized price, CAC, labor, insurance and specialist costs, margin, payback, and renewal; the £199-£699 monthly software benchmark constrains pricing unless managed value is clearly demonstrated.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: In-scope EU importers with material certificate exposure form an identifiable beachhead, but the 50-tonne exemption removes the vast majority of importers and concentrates demand among fewer, larger accounts. Regional account counts, spend, and sales-cycle lengths are unknown, weakening confidence that a narrow Polish or CEE wedge is both accessible and large enough.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: An integration-neutral decision layer could occupy a useful niche without replacing brokers, ERPs, registries, or verifiers. Nonetheless, the position is nonexclusive and replaceable, the business owns no customer relationship today, and CBAMable, brokers, CarbonChain, and SAP can add or bundle similar exposure comparisons, making segment dominance unlikely on the current structure.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Importer data mappings and exposure models could support additional CBAM categories, geographies, compliance monitoring, and adjacent trade-carbon decisions. Expansion is plausible but depends on first establishing customer access, lawful reuse rights, and repeatable economics, none of which is proven.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Potential retained mappings and benchmarks may improve delivery, but reuse rights are unsigned and no proprietary dataset, switching cost, exclusivity, network effect, or controlled regulatory function exists. Source data, verification, and the official registry remain externally controlled, while incumbents can copy or bundle the workflow.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The offer may reduce wasted supplier-collection and verification effort by first comparing defaults with actual-value economics, and its fixed scope is convenient. No supplied evidence quantifies superior savings, speed, accuracy, or usability relative to software, advisers, brokers, or ERP modules, so behavior-changing advantage remains hypothetical.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The definitive regime began in 2026, certificate prices create immediate financial exposure, and upcoming declarations support urgency. This favorable regulatory timing also attracts established vendors, while simplification has narrowed the customer pool.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Targeted importer outreach and adviser referrals are feasible experiments and do not require a personal brand. Still, there is no pipeline, signed referral partner, conversion evidence, or validated CAC; concentrated larger accounts may impose enterprise sales cycles, and brokers can white-label competing software and retain the relationship.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The analytical work fits the founder, can start with customer exports, needs modest capital, and fixed-scope pilots are compatible with part-time validation. Execution remains exposed to regulatory liability, cybersecurity, insurance, specialist oversight, data-quality variance, and potentially long sales cycles, while a 15-25 hour weekly commitment is near the founder's stated limit.

highest_value_structural_change: Secure a channel or workflow position that incumbents cannot cheaply displace, ideally a multi-year embedded partnership with a customs adviser, accountant network, or trade association that grants direct importer access, recurring data flows, and lawful rights to retain anonymized benchmarks; without this, the offer remains a copyable standalone service sold account by account.
main_structural_strength: The redesign makes supplier actual-emissions collection optional and centers a fixed-scope, importer-controlled economic decision, reducing dependence on supplier cooperation, verifier accreditation, and open-ended service labor.
primary_score_limiter: There is no demonstrated reason for importers to buy and renew a separate service at attractive fully loaded economics when defaults, low-priced specialist software, brokers, and SAP can cover or bundle much of the workflow.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: A direct substitute already offers evidence requests, audit history, regulatory exports, and broker white-labelling for £199-£699 per month, while SAP has announced an end-to-end bundled CBAM solution; together these directly undermine premium pricing, channel ownership, and defensibility for a standalone decision desk.
